question: site R18 requires the /start page's 'Create your team' button to be at least 44 px high and of the same control kind as the front page's primary button. The site job made it the front page's primary button (cs-btn primary): at 390 px it is 44+ px, but at 1280 px it is 40 px, because interface-assets' civicsmith.css sets cs-btn min-height 40px and its 44 px rule sits only under @media (max-width: 760px). The site cannot raise it alone without a second style source (site R9) or an inline style (CSP, site R8), and doing so would make it differ from the front page's button. Which: (A) interface-assets raises cs-btn's min-height to 44 px at every width (all primary buttons change), or (B) R18 is amended to require 44 px at phone width (390 px) only, 40 px on desktop as the visual language draws it? Recommend one, with the reason in the lane's own terms.

decision: Kept (BOB). (1) The ceremony screen files the edition's docket entry in the same sitting, right after caseratify answers committed: door op docketrecordedition prepare, sign the statement in NS_DOCKET with the same owner key, file; on DOCKET_STALE re-prepare and sign once; a failure is stated and never changes the ceremony's answer, and the entry stays core-due (R9(b)) for any owner to post from the docket page by the same op. docketPrepare drops the edition kind. (3) Edition 1 files an entry with what_changed null; R9(b) becomes each ratified edition. (4) No uses edge: ratification calls nothing of docket (K5571 (2)); the new op's door rows follow BD-1. Ratification F1 closes as met by design and moves to screens-publish R13 and docket R33/R9(b)/R32. Ratification F1 part 2, after Bob (6 Nov ~18:05Z, verbatim): 'If an edition is scheduled to be published, then shouldn't the edition be signed when that publication is scheduled?' Design signing at scheduling time so that nothing in the scheduled edition's docket entry goes unsigned: e.g. the owner signs the edition and its scheduled time when scheduling, and the entry binds that signature, with seq, previous and date settled so a peer can verify the chain. Say plainly: whether it needs a format change to docket R6/R24 or case-import R18; what a peer verifies; what happens if the schedule changes, the edition is cancelled, or the owner's key rotates or is revoked before publication; and how this interacts with the 60-minute staleness and the UTC-day binding. decision: F1 part 2 and AI-use provenance (publication lane, 6 Nov 18:08Z and 18:31Z; BOB accepts). Scheduled editions: at the sitting that signs publishat the owner signs the edition's docket entry as a complete entry (seq next, previous the head, date the UTC day of publish_at, document the waiting edition's doc_sha); docket holds it unpublished, one per case, and files it unchanged when the edition is published; discards it on stop or cancel; a move across UTC days re-signs it or discards it; any public entry placed on the case while one is held also re-signs the held entry at its new position in the same act (DOCKET_HELD_EDITION_UNSIGNED writes nothing); at filing docket checks previous is the head and document equals the published docSha, else the item falls to core-due (fallback A). Provenance: one format change, bio-case-document/11, per sentence of the case's own prose {ord, sid, text, cites, kind, bias_statement?, origin, draft?}, sid = first 16 hex of sha256(kind + "\n" + NFC text), origin one of human, ai_edited, ai_kept, declared_ai (IPTC digital-source-type mapping fixed in the format), review: {ratified_by, standard} once per edition; formats up to /10 read origin not_stated. The docket edition entry gains the additive field document (doc sha) in civicsmith-docket-entry/1. Producers: case-account per-sentence comparison, case-inputs field origins, wizard-scripts R27 acceptance records (field, draft, text sha), record-grammar R52 result link, case-authoring writes /11, case-catalogue new C-41.x, case-checker reads /11, public-read serves origin and review, docket R6/R33.
